# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 9 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_009_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 9

**9:1** Joseph, throwing down his adze, went also to meet them. When all were assembled, they went to the high priest, each man holding his staff. The high priest took all the staffs and went into the temple and prayed. When he had finished his prayer, he came out and returned the staffs, and there was no sign among them.

**9:2** Joseph received the last staff, and behold, a dove came out from the staff and flew onto Joseph's head. And the priest said to Joseph: "Joseph, you have been chosen by lot to take the virgin of the Lord into your keeping."

**9:3** But Joseph refused, saying: "I have sons already, and I am an old man, while she is a young girl. I shall be made a laughingstock among the children of Israel."

**9:4** And the priest said to Joseph: "Fear the Lord your God, and remember what God did to Dathan and Abiram and Korah — how the earth split open and swallowed them, because they resisted him. Fear now lest the same happen to your house, O Joseph."

**9:5** And Joseph, being afraid, took her into his keeping and said to her: "Mary, I have received you from the temple of the Lord. I now leave you in my house and go away to build my buildings. The Lord will watch over you. I will return to you."

---

## Translator's Note

Joseph's reluctance (9:3) — "I am an old man, and she is a young girl" — is the narrative foundation for the tradition that Joseph was an elderly widower. The author explicitly wants to protect Mary's virginity while explaining why the Gospels mention "brothers" of Jesus (they are Joseph's children from a previous marriage). The reference to Dathan, Abiram, and Korah (Num 16) invokes the paradigmatic punishment for resisting divine appointment.
